newsitem.title: USA: GATX Q4 tempered by GATX Terminals downturn.
newsitem.headline: GATX Q4 tempered by GATX Terminals downturn.

text.p: GATX Corp, posting slightly higher fourth-quarter earnings and record full-year net, said a downturn at its GATX Terminals business tempered its growth.
"Because of the downturn at GATX Terminals, GATX did not achieve as great a growth rate as we would have liked," said chairman Ronald Zech in a statement.
But he said strategies are in place for improving performance in 1997, and "we expect to again report improved net earnings for the year."

GATX Terminals, GATX's bulk-liquid storage, distribution and pipeline operation, reported fourth-quarter operating earnings of $1.4 million compared to $6.1 million a year ago. The 1996 quarter's results include costs related to employee terminations and costs to transform the company's competitive position.
The unit's full-year operating earnings fell to $12.6 milion from $31 million in 1995.

"We are obviously disappointed with the impact on GATX Terminals of the major changes underway in the petroleum industry. We have responded aggressively to those conditions, but it will take time for the marketplace to settle down and for the benefits of our actions to flow through to the bottom line," Zech said.

In November, GATX Terminals annunced a plan to realign its operations to meet changing customer needs. It did so by centralizing the organization which previously was structured geographically with highly autonomous units.
Meanwhile, Zech said GATX Capital showed "exceptional" performance. Its net operating income grew by more than 40 percent, reflecting strong rail, air and technology markets.
The company's General American Transportation unit also posted a record year, Zech said.
GATX reported fourth-quarter per-share earnings of $0.76, up from $0.75. For the year, primary per-share earnings were $4.37, up from $4.30 in 1995.
